title: Interview Case Studio and Skill Mosaic - 14d Lab
content:
Purpose:
This is a short, practical playbook for running a 14-day candidate assessment + starter-onboard experiment we're calling the "Interview Case Studio". Goal: surface signal for role fit beyond canned whiteboards, make candidate experience feel like real work, and create discrete evidence pockets we can use in the final hiring decision and Day 0 plan if hired.

Context / why this exists:
- Traditional interview loops surface algorithmic problem-solving and system design, but miss glue skills: product judgment, tradeoff framing, cross-team collaboration rhythm.
- We want a fast, repeatable way to simulate 1st-week work in a low-friction, respectful manner that also reduces bias by focusing on evidence.
- This doc blends 3 parts: short case assignment, a lightweight rubric (the "skill mosaic"), and an onboarding starter checklist if we extend an offer.

High-level flow (14 days):
Day 0-1: invite -> context pack + sample micro-dataset + scheduling options (candidate chooses 1-week or 2-week timeline)
Day 2-6: candidate works on case studio asynchronously (5–10 hours max recommended). We provide a small dataset or repo and 3 prompts of differing focus (design, debugging, communication synthesis).
Day 7: touchpoint call (30–45m) with hiring manager and peer reviewer — collegial discussion, not grilling.
Day 8-10: internal scoring and calibration meeting (panel reads evidence pockets; we capture notes in the matrix)
Day 11-14: optional trial task extension for borderline candidates (short pairing session or refined follow-up).

What we give to candidates: the "Studio Pack"
- One-pager context: product goals, constraints, success metrics
- Minimal reproducible dataset or small repo (anonymized logs or a mocked API)
- 3 prompts (pick 1 or do all):
  1) Tradeoff memo: propose two approaches and a rollout plan (max 600 words)
  2) Debug diary: given failing testcases, outline investigation steps + quick patch sketch (pseudocode ok)
  3) Collaborative spec: write a short RFC for a non-trivial edge case, include test plan + rollout notes
- Explicit instructions on time budget (aim for 5–10 hours), deliverable formats (md, pdf, link), and accessibility accommodations options

Scoring: Skill Mosaic (single-page rubric) — keep it lightweight, evidence-oriented
We score each dimension 0-3 (0 = no signal, 3 = strong evidence). Add brief evidence note per dimension. Dimensions:
- Problem Framing and Prioritization
- Technical Correctness & Pragmatism
- Product Judgment / Outcome focus
- Collaboration Signals (clarity in writing, plan for handoff)
- Quality & Test Thinking
- Communication & Stakeholder Empathy
- Learning Velocity (how they approach unknowns)
- Cultural Fit Signals (brief behavioral evidence)

Scoring guidance (panel notes):
- Use concrete excerpts: quote the memo where they prioritized a constraint, or call out a specific test they included. Avoid global adjectives.
- If evidence is conflicting between reviewers, capture precise disagreement in calibration notes (e.g., "Tech correctness: reviewer A found a logic gap in X; reviewer B thought it was acceptable given timeboxed tradeoff").

Panel calibration template (what to capture in the 1-hr readout):
- 3 biggest strengths (short bullets)
- 2 clear risks + mitigations (how we might onboard to reduce the risk)
- Recommendation (hire / no-hire / trial-extension), with vote + one-sentence rationale

Onboarding starter checklist (if we hire): Day 0-9 condensed starter to help candidate land fast and reduce first-week uncertainty
Day 0 (pre-boarding): access requests queued (GitHub, Slack, infra read-only), intro to Studio pack repository, mentor assigned
Day 1: 60m intro with manager (context, success metrics), 30m with mentor for dev environment setup, set 3-week success goals
Day 2-3: small warm tasks (one bug + one docs improvement) derived from candidate's case studio to preserve continuity
Day 4-5: pair with peer on a small feature toggle and deploy to staging, end-of-week sync with manager
Day 6-9: owner of a micro-project with clear acceptance criteria (safe scope) and a public retrospective at day 9

Operational notes and fairness guardrails:
- Offer candidates an explicit opt-out for any asynchronous take-home. Provide a timed pairing alternative.
- Compensate select long-form Studio work for >10 hours (stipend) — standardize stipend amount (TBD) and approvals.
- Ensure anonymization of any customer data. Work with privacy to scrub or synthesize datasets.
- Keep timebox guidance visible in the pack. Encourage candidates to surface tradeoffs they did not implement.

Sample rubrics snippets (how reviewers should write evidence):
- Problem framing (2): "Explicitly prioritized latency over cost for high-frequency endpoints, cited 95th pct latency target; proposed caching layer and graceful degradation — evidence: memo para 2"
- Communication (3): "Extensive comments on tests and rollout; included a README with clear next steps and responsible parties"

Unresolved questions / backlog items (notes to self):
- Decide stipend threshold and amount (ask finance/people-ops). Jira: HR-1428 assigned to Samir.
- Add standardized accessibility language for Studio pack (Lina).
- Track candidate conversion rate from Studio -> offer -> accept to judge experience friction. Metric owner: Jon (spreadsheet link in linked_artifacts).

Experiment hypothesis (for this 14d run):
- H1: Studio reduces on-site panel time by 40% while maintaining hiring quality (measured by 90-day ramp retention and manager satisfaction)
- H2: Candidates appreciate the Studio format for real-signal hiring; net promoter score > 70 among participants

Quick checklist for running a Studio loop (People Ops owner + Hiring Manager):
- [ ] Approve Studio pack and dataset (privacy sign-off)
- [ ] Decide stipend and scheduling window
- [ ] Assign 2 reviewers + hiring manager for calibration
- [ ] Create candidate folder + internal evidence template in Drive
- [ ] Schedule calibration meeting 48–72 hours after submission

Notes to reviewer (tone & style):
- Be generous and specific. Cite the exact artifact line that supports your score. Avoid gut-only statements.
- Respect candidate time. If a submission is clearly off-track, document why and recommend a short follow-up call rather than an extended written ask.

Appendix: example Studio prompt (engineer infra-focused)
You are joining a seeded feature that serves inference for a small set of customers. Latency SLO 200ms p95, cost target $X per 1k requests. Given logs (attached), propose a plan to diagnose a recent latency regression, recommend 2 short-term mitigations and 1 medium-term change. Deliver: 1) 1-page memo, 2) one test-plan bullet list, 3) short pseudo-patch sketch or script.

---
Action items after this run:
- Consolidate stipend policy and publish in Studio pack (owner: Samir)
- Build a template Drive folder for candidate evidence with the rubric matrix pre-filled (owner: Lina)
- Run 6 pilot loops in Q1 and collect NPS + hiring outcome metrics (owner: Jon)

Notes to self: this doc is meant to be a living playbook. Expect iterations after 2 pilot cohorts. Keep the language simple and accessible.
